    The text is written in black font on a white background and reads: 
    "Other people who help us besides our parents: our teachers, our mentors, our friends, our colleagues. God, what is there to say about Andy Van Dam? When I was a freshman at Brown, he was on leave. And all I heard about was this Andy Van Dam. He was like a mythical creature. Like a centaur, but like a really pissed off centaur. And everybody was like really sad that he was gone, but kind of more relaxed? And I found out why. Because I started working for Andy. I was a teaching assistant for him as a sophomore. title: Bobby McFerrin, but make it a life philosophy
summary:
The line that kept getting quoted like scripture: Visa (@visakanv) watching Bobby McFerrin turn a random crowd into his backing track and concluding that “*everybody* gets to have so much more fun if you involve the audience.” He’s not just fangirling the musical trick—he’s treating it as a blueprint for how to teach, collaborate, build communities, and even do “good reply game”: your job is “to make him sound better.”

The whole thing kicks off when Visa reposts the 2009 World Science Festival clip in June 2020 and does a play-by-play of McFerrin’s technique: surprise them (add the 3rd note), challenge them, let them laugh, then bring them back—“facts + sensitivity,” as he later ties it to Neil deGrasse Tyson’s critique of Dawkins. Malcolm Ocean (@Malcolm_Ocean) adds a key detail—McFerrin explains it without words—while the replies peak in pure Twitter mode: “when you can’t afford a loop pedal but u have a village,” “its like getting only the good parts of a cult.” Within days Visa generalizes it into the mantra “make stuff and involve people,” pointing to street artist Aheneah recruiting locals to finish murals, and Samin Nosrat roping friends into cooking as a gift.

Then it refuses to die. Over 2021–2024 Visa keeps re-quoting the same McFerrin clip as the anchor for bigger claims: audience-building can be “positive-sum” if you have clarity, asking for help is a “cheat code” if you give people discrete ways to contribute, and most people just need a supportive learning environment (which school usually isn’t, but some corners of Twitter can be). The funniest full-circle payoff: in 2023 Malcolm Ocean actually gets onstage and improv-sings with Bobby McFerrin—basically the thread manifesting in real life. Why care? Because it’s a deceptively simple model for leadership without coercion: create structure, invite participation, and people will do way more than you think—joyfully.
